meta_description: Connected imaging fleets with predictive service — uptime up 3.4 points and emergency engineer dispatch down 41%

blocks.x: Connected imaging fleets with predictive service — uptime up 3.4 points and emergency engineer dispatch down 41%

Identity withheld — a device maker whose imaging fleets were serviced on calendar and whose hospital customers measured uptime in surgical-schedule impact. Figures are the client's own, shared with permission.
The baseline quarter counted the calendar's cost: 91.2% fleet uptime, 38% of service visits finding no fault, and tube replacements scheduled by age while failures happened by usage.
Device telemetry existed but landed in per-product silos; nobody could see a fleet, let alone predict one. Service parts traveled on forecast, not on condition.

We connected the fleet as a twin: telemetry normalized across product lines into one fleet model, failure signatures learned per subsystem with service engineers labeling ground truth, parts pre-positioned by predicted need, and the hospital-facing portal showing exactly what the service organization sees. The twin now runs dispatch, not just dashboards.
